key_insight: A scalar-conditioned sequence-to-sequence deep learning model can accurately predict the full time-resolved adhesive force history of viscoelastic Hertzian contacts from displacement input, spanning both short- and long-range adhesion regimes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a fast surrogate for expensive contact simulations, enabling real-time soft robotics control, gripping/manipulation design, and optimization loops.
method: Trained stateful sequence models to map prescribed displacement histories to complete force trajectories.
Used a fixed-measurement-step (FMS) representation to handle variable-rate, variable-length time histories across wide time scales.
Compared LSTM, TCN, and time-distributed dense architectures with different Tabor-parameter conditioning strategies.
evidence_signal: The dataset spans four orders of magnitude in loading/unloading rates and dwell times with Tabor parameter 0.2–3.2; the best model achieved held-out MSE of 5.0×10^-4, median pull-off-force error of ~2.2%, median hysteresis error of ~1.1%, and median inference time of 0.16 s.
watch_item: Performance depends on the training domain and the FMS time representation, so extrapolation to new material laws, geometries, or loading protocols beyond the sampled parameter space may require retraining or validation.
paper_title: Deep learning-based prediction of time-resolved adhesive forces in viscoelastic Hertzian contacts
